questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UNFCCC:
1. It was adopted at the Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992.
2. It entered into force in 1994.
3. Its secretariat is located in Geneva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Convention was adopted at Rio in 1992 and came into force on 21 March 1994 after enough ratifications. Its secretariat is in Bonn, Germany, not Geneva.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter
questions.h: Rio 1992 opens it, 1994 starts it, Bonn hosts it.

questions.q:
With reference to the Kyoto Protocol, consider the following statements:
1. It set binding emission reduction targets for developed countries listed in Annex I.
2. India had a binding emission reduction target in the first commitment period.
3. The United States ratified the Protocol but withdrew in 2001.
4. It entered into force in 2005.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Developing countries such as India, being non-Annex I, had no binding targets because of CBDR. The US signed the Protocol but never ratified it, so it was never bound.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Match List-I (Kyoto mechanism) with List-II (feature):
List-I
A. Clean Development Mechanism
B. Joint Implementation
C. International Emissions Trading
List-II
1. Annex I countries trade assigned amount units among themselves
2. Project in a developing country earns Certified Emission Reductions
3. Annex I country earns Emission Reduction Units from a project in another Annex I country
questions.e: CDM (Article 12) links developed and developing countries through CERs. Joint Implementation (Article 6) works between two Annex I parties through ERUs. Emissions trading (Article 17) moves assigned amount units between Annex I parties.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter
questions.h: CDM = Credit from Developing; JI = Joint between Industrialised.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Unlike the Kyoto Protocol, the Paris Agreement obliges all parties, including developing countries, to prepare and communicate nationally determined contributions.
Statement-II: The Paris Agreement sets legally binding national emission reduction targets for every party.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Under Paris, every party must submit successive NDCs (a binding procedural obligation), but the level of the target is nationally determined and not legally binding. Kyoto, by contrast, imposed top-down targets only on Annex I parties.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following was the first institutional arrangement under the UNFCCC process to address loss and damage associated with climate change impacts?
o: Fund for responding to Loss and Damage
questions.e: The Warsaw International Mechanism was set up at COP19 (2013). The Santiago Network came later at COP25 (2019) to give technical help, and the loss and damage fund was agreed at COP27 (2022).
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
India's updated Nationally Determined Contribution (2022) includes which of the following?
1. Reducing the emissions intensity of GDP by 45 per cent by 2030 from the 2005 level.
2. Achieving about 50 per cent cumulative electric power installed capacity from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030.
3. Achieving net-zero emissions by 2050.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The 2022 update raised the 2015 goals of 33-35 per cent intensity cut and 40 per cent non-fossil capacity to 45 per cent and about 50 per cent. India's net-zero year is 2070, not 2050.
questions.s: PIB, Aug 2022 (updated NDC)

questions.q:
Consider the following targets announced by India at COP26 in Glasgow (the Panchamrit):
1. 500 GW of non-fossil energy capacity by 2030.
2. Net-zero emissions by 2070.
3. Reduction of the carbon intensity of the economy by 20 per cent by 2030.
4. Reduction of projected carbon emissions by one billion tonnes by 2030.
How many of the above are correct?
questions.e: The carbon intensity target announced was below 45 per cent by 2030, not 20 per cent. The other three are genuine; the fifth element was meeting 50 per cent of energy requirements from renewables by 2030.
questions.s: PIB, 2 Nov 2021

questions.q: India announced the goal of reaching net-zero emissions by 2070 at which Conference of the Parties?
questions.e: Prime Minister Modi announced the Panchamrit, including net-zero by 2070, at Glasgow in November 2021. India's updated NDC and long-term strategy followed in 2022.
questions.s: PIB, 2 Nov 2021

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR):
1. It finds place in Principle 7 of the Rio Declaration and Article 3 of the UNFCCC.
2. It implies that all countries have identical obligations to cut emissions.
3. It expects developed countries to take the lead in combating climate change.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CBDR recognises a common responsibility but different obligations because developed countries contributed most to historic emissions and have more resources. It therefore rejects identical obligations, and developed parties are asked to take the lead.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Statement-I: Under the UNFCCC, only Annex II parties are obliged to provide financial resources to developing countries.
Statement-II: Annex II consists of developed country parties that were OECD members in 1992, excluding economies in transition.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Annex II is the subset of Annex I made up of OECD members of 1992, leaving out economies in transition. Because they have the means, the Convention places the duty of financing and technology transfer on them, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
With reference to loss and damage in climate negotiations, consider the following statements:
1. The Warsaw International Mechanism was established at COP19.
2. Article 8 of the Paris Agreement recognises the importance of averting, minimising and addressing loss and damage.
3. The decision to set up a fund for loss and damage was taken at COP26, Glasgow.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The fund was agreed at COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh (2022) and operationalised at COP28 in Dubai. At Glasgow, developed countries blocked a fund and only agreed to a dialogue, which is why the fund came a year later.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the International Solar Alliance (ISA):
1. Membership is permanently restricted to countries lying between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.
2. It was launched by India and France on the sidelines of COP21 in Paris.
3. Its headquarters is in Gurugram, India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The ISA was launched in November 2015 at Paris and is headquartered in Gurugram. Its framework agreement was amended so that all UN member states can join, so the tropical-belt restriction no longer holds.
questions.s: MoNRE / ISA website; Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q: The Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) was launched by India at
o: the Sendai Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction, 2015
the UN Climate Action Summit, New York, 2019
questions.e: Prime Minister Modi announced CDRI at the UN Climate Action Summit in September 2019. It is a partnership of countries and organisations working on resilience of infrastructure to climate and disaster risks, with its secretariat in New Delhi.
questions.s: PIB, 23 Sep 2019

questions.q:
Match List-I (COP) with List-II (outcome):
List-I
A. COP13, Bali
B. COP16, Cancun
C. COP19, Warsaw
D. COP26, Glasgow
List-II
1. Green Climate Fund established
2. Bali Action Plan
3. Warsaw International Mechanism
4. Phase-down of unabated coal power called for
questions.e: Bali (2007) produced the Bali Action Plan, Cancun (2010) established the Green Climate Fund, Warsaw (2013) the loss and damage mechanism, and Glasgow (2021) the first COP text mentioning coal.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter
questions.h: B-B, C-C, W-W, G-G: Bali Plan, Cancun Capital fund, Warsaw loss, Glasgow coal.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order of their adoption:
1. Bali Action Plan
2. Kyoto Protocol
3. Cancun Agreements
4. Warsaw International Mechanism
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Kyoto came in 1997, Bali in 2007, Cancun in 2010 and Warsaw in 2013. Each COP built on the failure of the previous design: Bali started the post-Kyoto talks, Cancun brought the Copenhagen pledges into the UN system.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the classification of countries under the UNFCCC:
1. Annex I includes OECD countries and economies in transition.
2. Non-Annex I parties are mostly developing countries.
3. India is an Annex I party.
4. Annex II is a subset of Annex I.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India is a Non-Annex I party, so statement 3 is wrong. Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the entry into force of the Paris Agreement:
1. It required ratification by at least 55 parties accounting for at least 55 per cent of total global greenhouse gas emissions.
2. It required ratification by all Annex II countries.
3. It entered into force on 4 November 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 55/55 threshold was crossed in October 2016, with India's ratification on 2 October helping, and the Agreement came into force a month later. No special role was demanded of Annex II countries.
questions.s: UNFCCC; Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Global Stocktake under the Paris Agreement:
1. It is provided for in Article 14.
2. It is conducted every five years.
3. Its first cycle concluded at COP26, Glasgow.
4. It assesses collective progress towards the long-term goals of the Agreement.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The first Global Stocktake concluded at COP28 in Dubai (2023), not at Glasgow. The rest are correct. Its output is meant to inform the next round of NDCs.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the six greenhouse gases covered by the Kyoto Protocol in its first commitment period?
questions.e: The basket was CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs and SF6. CFCs were already controlled under the Montreal Protocol because they deplete ozone, so Kyoto left them out to avoid double regulation.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following funds is financed in part by a share of the proceeds from Clean Development Mechanism project activities?
questions.e: The Adaptation Fund was set up under the Kyoto Protocol and gets a 2 per cent share of proceeds of CERs issued for CDM projects. The GCF depends on contributions from countries.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Green Climate Fund (GCF):
1. It was established at COP16 in Cancun in 2010.
2. Its headquarters is in Songdo, South Korea.
3. It serves as an operating entity of the financial mechanism of the UNFCCC.
4. It is hosted and administered by the World Bank as its permanent trustee body.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The GCF is an independent institution headquartered in Songdo. The World Bank is only its interim trustee, so statement 4 is wrong.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Statement-I: Developing countries including India argue that developed countries should bear greater responsibility for climate action.
Statement-II: The stock of carbon dioxide accumulated in the atmosphere is largely the result of industrialisation in developed countries since the nineteenth century.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: India's equity argument rests on cumulative, historical emissions, not annual flows today. Because developed countries emitted most in the past while developing their economies, they are expected to lead and to finance, which is what CBDR says.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment; UNFCCC Art 3

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. BASIC is a grouping of Brazil, South Africa, India and China on climate negotiations.
2. The Alliance of Small Island States (AOSIS) represents the interests of low-lying island countries vulnerable to sea level rise.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: BASIC took shape around the 2009 Copenhagen negotiations. AOSIS pushes for the 1.5 degree Celsius limit because for its members rising seas are an existential threat.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q: At COP29 in Baku, the New Collective Quantified Goal on climate finance asked developed countries to take the lead in mobilising at least how much per year by 2035?
questions.e: The 100 billion goal was the earlier target for 2020-2025. Baku raised it to 300 billion by 2035, while a wider call was made for all actors to scale up to 1.3 trillion per year.
questions.s: UNFCCC COP29 outcome, Nov 2024

questions.q:
Match List-I (Article of the Paris Agreement) with List-II (subject):
List-I
A. Article 4
B. Article 6
C. Article 8
D. Article 14
List-II
1. Global stocktake
2. Nationally determined contributions
3. Loss and damage
4. Voluntary cooperative approaches and market mechanisms
questions.e: Article 4 covers NDCs, Article 6 covers cooperative approaches (carbon markets), Article 8 covers loss and damage and Article 14 the global stocktake.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q: The Kyoto Protocol could enter into force in February 2005 only after the emission threshold was met through ratification by which country?
questions.e: Entry into force needed 55 parties, including Annex I parties accounting for at least 55 per cent of Annex I carbon dioxide emissions in 1990. With the US outside, Russia's ratification in late 2004 pushed the total over the line.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following countries announced its withdrawal from the Kyoto Protocol in December 2011?
questions.e: Canada, facing costly targets it was far from meeting, withdrew with effect from December 2012. Japan and Russia stayed in but did not take targets in the second commitment period.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q: The Glasgow Climate Pact was the first COP decision to explicitly call for
o: a ban on new coal power plants worldwide
transitioning away from all fossil fuels
phasing down unabated coal power and phasing out inefficient fossil fuel subsidies
a global carbon tax on fossil fuels
questions.e: After a last-minute intervention led by India, the draft wording was softened from phase-out of coal to phase-down of unabated coal power. The 'transition away from fossil fuels' wording came later, at COP28.
questions.s: UNFCCC COP26 outcome, Nov 2021
questions.h: Glasgow = Coal down; Dubai = Fossil away.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about COP28 held in Dubai in 2023:
1. Its outcome called for the phase-out of all fossil fuels by 2050.
2. It concluded the first Global Stocktake.
3. It operationalised the fund for responding to loss and damage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The decision called for 'transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems' in a just and orderly manner, not for a dated phase-out of all fossil fuels. The loss and damage fund was operationalised on the opening day.
questions.s: UNFCCC COP28 outcome, Dec 2023

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's climate commitments:
1. India's first INDC was submitted in 2015 and proposed to cut emissions intensity of GDP by 33 to 35 per cent by 2030 from the 2005 level.
2. The 2022 update raised this goal to 45 per cent.
3. The 2022 update changed the baseline year from 2005 to 2010.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The baseline stayed at 2005. Both the 2015 and 2022 targets are measured against the 2005 level of emission intensity.
questions.s: PIB, Aug 2022 (updated NDC)

questions.q: 'Mission LiFE', promoted by India, primarily seeks to
o: encourage mindful and deliberate use of resources through individual and community behaviour change
set up a global fund for coal plant retirement
create a carbon market for forest-based credits
questions.e: LiFE stands for Lifestyle for Environment. It replaces 'mindless and destructive consumption' with 'mindful and deliberate utilisation' and was presented at COP26 and launched formally in October 2022.
questions.s: PIB, 20 Oct 2022

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the eight missions under India's National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)?
o: National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem
questions.e: The NAPCC, released in 2008, has eight missions: Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture and Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change. Clean Ganga is a separate mission under the Jal Shakti ministry.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission:
1. It was launched in 2010 as one of the missions under the NAPCC.
2. Its target was later raised from 20 GW to 100 GW of solar capacity by 2022.
3. The 100 GW target was to include 40 GW of rooftop solar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The mission started with 20,000 MW by 2022 and in 2015 the target was quintupled to 100 GW, split between 60 GW utility-scale and 40 GW rooftop. These were targets and not actual achievements by 2022.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about domestic carbon market regulation in India:
1. The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022 enables the Central Government to specify a carbon credit trading scheme.
2. The Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme operates under the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency.
3. The Act amended the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 to create carbon credits.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2022 amendment was made to the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, not the EPA 1986. PAT, run by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency, trades energy savings certificates among designated industries.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT an outcome of the Rio Earth Summit of 1992?
questions.e: The UNCCD was adopted in 1994, two years later, as a follow-up to a Rio call. Rio itself gave the UNFCCC, the CBD, the Rio Declaration, Agenda 21 and the Forest Principles.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Statement-I: Hydrofluorocarbons are being phased down under the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol.
Statement-II: Hydrofluorocarbons have high global warming potential even though they do not deplete the ozone layer.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: HFCs replaced CFCs and HCFCs, which saved the ozone layer but trapped heat strongly. The 2016 Kigali Amendment therefore uses an ozone treaty to cut a climate pollutant.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Montreal Protocol

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about nationally determined contributions (NDCs):
1. Each successive NDC is expected to represent a progression beyond the party's previous one.
2. The Paris Agreement provides for financial penalties for countries that miss their NDC targets.
3. Parties are to communicate NDCs every five years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The compliance mechanism of the Paris Agreement is facilitative and non-punitive. The 'ratchet' works by peer pressure and transparency, not fines.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Paris Agreement is described as a bottom-up approach to climate action.
Statement-II: Each party determines its own contribution under the Paris Agreement.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Kyoto's targets were negotiated and assigned top-down to Annex I. Paris lets every party set its own NDC, and that national choice is exactly what makes the architecture bottom-up.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Match List-I (Negotiating group) with List-II (description):
List-I
A. AOSIS
B. BASIC
C. Umbrella Group
D. LMDC
List-II
1. Coalition of low-lying island nations
2. Brazil, South Africa, India, China
3. Loose coalition of non-EU developed countries
4. Developing countries stressing equity and CBDR, including India and China
questions.e: These are the standard negotiating blocs. The Umbrella Group includes countries such as Australia, Canada, Japan and the US, while LMDC (Like-Minded Developing Countries) argues for equity.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The World Bank is an operating entity of the financial mechanism of the UNFCCC.
2. The Global Environment Facility is an operating entity of the financial mechanism of the UNFCCC.
3. The Green Climate Fund is an operating entity of the financial mechanism of the UNFCCC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Convention entrusted its financial mechanism to the GEF and later the GCF. The World Bank only serves as trustee or host for several funds and is not itself an operating entity.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q: India's NDC commits to creating an additional carbon sink of 2.5 to 3 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030 through
questions.e: Forests and trees absorb carbon dioxide, and the sink target dates from India's 2015 INDC and was retained in the 2022 update.
questions.s: PIB, Aug 2022 (updated NDC)

questions.q: The second commitment period of the Kyoto Protocol, under the Doha Amendment, covers the years
questions.e: The first period ran 2008-2012. At Doha (COP18, 2012) the Protocol was extended for 2013-2020, but with fewer countries bound, which is why Paris was needed.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following negotiating mandates led directly to the Paris Agreement?
questions.e: COP17 at Durban (2011) set up a process to develop a new legal instrument applicable to all, to be adopted by 2015 and implemented from 2020. The Paris Agreement is its product.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q: The term 'Intended Nationally Determined Contributions' was first introduced when parties were invited to prepare them at
questions.e: Warsaw (2013) invited parties to start domestic preparations for INDCs ahead of Paris. Lima then elaborated what information they should contain, and they became NDCs once a party ratified the Paris Agreement.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy:
1. It was submitted to the UNFCCC at COP27 in 2022.
2. It sets 2050 as the year for net-zero emissions.
3. Parties are encouraged to formulate such strategies under Article 4 of the Paris Agreement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The strategy follows Article 4(19) and is anchored on the 2070 net-zero goal, matching the Glasgow announcement.
questions.s: PIB, Nov 2022

questions.q:
Match List-I (Indian initiative) with List-II (focus):
List-I
A. International Solar Alliance
B. Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure
C. Mission LiFE
D. One Sun One World One Grid
List-II
1. Behavioural change towards sustainable consumption
2. Solar-rich countries working together to scale up solar energy
3. Resilience of infrastructure to climate and disaster risks
4. Transnational interconnected solar power grid
questions.e: These are India-led global initiatives. ISA gathers sunshine countries, CDRI covers infrastructure, LiFE changes habits and OSOWOG imagines a shared solar grid across regions.
questions.s: PIB; Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q: The term 'net-zero emissions' refers to a situation in which
o: no greenhouse gas is released by any activity
a country emits only gases that are not greenhouse gases
greenhouse gases released by human activity are balanced by the amount removed from the atmosphere
emissions are fully offset by buying credits from another country alone
questions.e: Net-zero allows residual emissions so long as they are cancelled by removals such as forests, soil carbon or technological capture. It is not a promise of literally zero emissions.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Cancun Agreements (2010):
1. They set up a fund for loss and damage.
2. They established the Green Climate Fund.
3. They set up a Technology Mechanism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Cancun established the GCF and the Technology Mechanism and brought the Copenhagen pledges into the UN process. Loss and damage had to wait until Warsaw (mechanism, 2013) and Sharm el-Sheikh (fund, 2022).
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Copenhagen Accord of 2009:
1. It was negotiated at COP15 and was only 'taken note of' by the COP, not formally adopted.
2. It contained a pledge by developed countries to mobilise USD 100 billion a year by 2020.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Accord was a political deal brokered by a few leaders and not formally adopted, which is why its contents were later folded into the Cancun Agreements. The 100 billion pledge was its most lasting element.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following is a legally binding feature of the Paris Agreement for every party?
o: Achieving the exact NDC target in full by 2030
Paying a carbon tax into the Green Climate Fund
Preparing, communicating and maintaining successive NDCs
questions.e: Parties must prepare, communicate and maintain NDCs and pursue domestic measures to meet them, but the outcome is not guaranteed by law. This blend is why the Agreement could secure near-universal participation.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change chapter
